text:
nick harper: heads-up - customer noticed a "console flash" where a few cards from a different org appeared after hammering the org switch button. can repro locally. :grimacing:

olga petrov: can you share steps and cluster?

nick harper: repro on canary-3 with the new prefetch sidecar. steps: login org-blue -> quick switch to org-green -> switch back to org-blue immediately. about 1-3% of runs show 2 cards from org-green stuck in the sidepanel while header shows org-blue.

dinesh varma: likely the prefetch sidecar is "sideloading" auth metadata at enqueue time. the sidecar workers snapshot headers into the job envelope and then later rehydrate exactly those headers. if session rotates the UI header and rendered context mismatch.

olga petrov: did you capture a trace?

nick harper: pasted a short trace: 
```
[2026-01-10T19:05:01Z] ui enqueues prefetch job id=pf-909 headers={"x-tenant":"org-blue","cookie":"s-901"}
[2026-01-10T19:05:01Z] quick-switch -> org-green user=acct-22
[2026-01-10T19:05:02Z] session rotated cookie s-901 -> s-902 org=org-green
[2026-01-10T19:05:02Z] sidecar worker pf-909 runs with envelope.headers.x-tenant=org-blue -> returns cards(org-blue)
[2026-01-10T19:05:02Z] ui merges returned cards into current list (header shows org-green) -> mixed tenant rows
```

dinesh varma: this also leaks into telemetry: dashboard aggregates spike as if both orgs contributed. and quota attribution may charge the wrong tenant if the background call increments usage metrics.

olga petrov: actionable options (short/medium/long):
- short: at sidecar start, always re-resolve session id from the cookie before making network calls. treat any envelope tenant header as advisory only. emit metric `sideload_mismatch_count` when mismatch detected.
- medium: disallow serializing tenant-identifying headers into job envelopes; store only a session reference and resolve at runtime. add migration sweep for existing envelopes older than 12h.
- long: deprecate sidecar header snapshots; move to server-side on-demand prefetch with strong request-scoped auth context.

nick harper: short option is lowest risk. please also add a UI safety UX: when we detect a mismatch while merging, show a subtle banner "Refreshing view to ensure tenant accuracy" while re-fetch completes so users aren't confused. small text and low friction.

dinesh varma: implementation sketch for short fix: 
```
// sidecar worker entry
const session = await sessionStore.resolve(job.envelope.sessionId)
if (!session) { log.warn(...); continue }
if (job.envelope.headers['x-tenant'] !== session.tenant) {
  metrics.increment('sideload_mismatch_count')
  // ignore stale header and re-fetch with resolved tenant
  await fetchWithTenant(session.tenant)
} else {
  await fetchWithTenant(session.tenant)
}
```

olga petrov: please make the mismatch metric include tags: {expected: job.envelope.headers['x-tenant'], resolved: session.tenant, age_s: job.envelope.age_seconds}. we'll use that to tune rollout and identify stale job blobs.

nick harper: testing plan: add a unit test that simulates mid-queue session rotation and an integration smoke that does 200 quick-switch loops. Gate the PR on the smoke passing. Add a canary rollout at 5% traffic.

dinesh varma: also add a billing safety check: if worker emits mismatch and then records usage, include the resolved tenant in the usage log and mark `attribution_corrected=true` so billing pipeline can reconcile. we should run a short backfill to detect any misattributions in the last 48h.

olga petrov: agreed. I'll own the PR: feature flag `sidecar_resolve_session_on_start` default ON for canary. include a migration sweep that re-enqueues envelopes older than 12h and tags them `requeued_for_session_resolve`. add rollout notes and a revert step.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch fix/sidecar-session-resolve - unit(21), integration(4).

deploy-bot: Deploying fix/sidecar-session-resolve to canary-3 (5% traffic) at 2026-01-10T19:20:00Z

olga petrov: watch memory and latency - re-resolving session at start adds a small latency but should be negligible compared to the prefetch calls. ops: please monitor sidecar P95 and pod RSS.

dinesh varma: after initial canary run (500 quick switches) mismatch metric dropped from 2.1/min -> 0.0/min. three old envelopes were requeued and fixed. queued a billing reconciliation job for the last 48h.

nick harper: thanks everyone. once billing confirms no material mischarges we can roll to production. tagging #release-war-room and #support with notes. :thumbsup:
